$comment: Registry for the model benchmark workflow (.github/workflows/eval-benchmark.yml), separate from e2e/matrix.json so adding a benchmark model never adds a CI check. `models` are slots: a stable `name` (`<lab>-high`, `-mid`, and `-low` tiers per major lab where the lab offers a current model for the tier, plus each open-weight family's main model; `openai-low` is eve's default model) and the gateway `id` that currently fills it. Bump a slot's `id` when its lab ships a successor; records keep both, and the pinned release marks the change. Leave out service-tier variants (`-fast`) unless they are eve's default. Each slot runs every listed fixture `attempts` times against the local world; each id must exist in the AI Gateway catalog, which pins its release. `mockWorlds` run each `mockFixtures` entry (default: every fixture) `mockAttempts` times with mock models (`local`, or a world with a package in e2e/matrix.json); mock legs cost only runner time, and their timings are the primary framework-overhead signal. Leave out of `mockFixtures` any fixture whose evals are all tagged `real-model`, since its mock legs would run nothing. `devStartup` runs `eve dev` startup `runs` times for a minimal agent and for each other tool count. `concurrency.legs` caps live legs running at once (gateway load); `concurrency.evalsPerLeg` is passed to `eve eval --max-concurrency` on every leg, overriding a fixture's own maxConcurrency, so evals do not share a runner. Both change measured latency, and each run's manifest records them.
